# Client Data Extracts

::: {.callout-important}
## Contractor access required

These extracts are provisioned for **active consulting engagements only**.
They are not part of CloudCore's public portfolio. Log in with your
engagement credentials to download.
:::

The four files below are the **operational data extracts** referenced in your
engagement brief. They describe the **same 280 CloudCore customers**, joined on
`customer_id`, so a finding in one file can be checked against the others.
Each file is small (280 rows or fewer, no missing values) and loads directly
into an Orange **File** widget or `pandas.read_csv()`.

| File | Rows | Contents |
|------|-----:|----------|
| [`cloudcore_customers.csv`](data/cloudcore_customers.csv) | 280 | Customer profile, tenure, product mix, churn flag |
| [`cloudcore_transactions.csv`](data/cloudcore_transactions.csv) | 280 | Usage and billing signals (2026-05 snapshot) |
| [`cloudcore_support_tickets.csv`](data/cloudcore_support_tickets.csv) | 360 | Ticket text, product, region, satisfaction |
| [`cloudcore_reviews.csv`](data/cloudcore_reviews.csv) | 240 | Free-text product reviews and ratings |

::: {.callout-note}
## These extracts, not the public portfolio

CloudCore also publishes a public [data portfolio](/data-dictionary.html)
(financial disclosures and market-facing figures). That portfolio is **not**
the operational data for your engagement: different reporting basis, different
figures. Quote the client's public numbers only when the brief asks for
market context; analyse the extracts on this page for everything else.
:::

## `cloudcore_customers.csv`

One row per customer. The customer master table.

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `customer_id` | string (key) | Stable identifier, `C0001`-`C0280`. Join key for all other files. |
| `company_name` | string | Customer name (quasi-identifier; treat as re-identifiable). |
| `industry` | categorical (9) | Finance, Healthcare, Retail, Manufacturing, Technology, Education, Logistics, Energy, Media. |
| `region` | categorical (3) | `Sydney`, `Singapore`, `San Francisco`. |
| `tenure_months` | numeric (int) | Months since onboarding, 1-60. |
| `products` | string | Product mix joined by ` + ` (e.g. `DataVault + CloudSync`). |
| `monthly_recurring_revenue` | numeric (USD) | Current MRR. Equals `billing_amount` in the transactions file. |
| `support_tier` | ordinal (4) | `Basic` < `Standard` < `Premium` < `Enterprise`. |
| `churn_flag` | binary (0/1) | 1 = churned or flagged at-risk in the observation window. About 25% positive. |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Signal worth finding

Churn is a **combination**, not a lookup. One region churns at roughly
two-to-three times the rate of the others; `support_tier` and `tenure_months`
carry strong signal but also correlate with spend. Product count is not
ready-made: it must be derived from the `products` string. No single column
separates churners from everyone else.
:::

## `cloudcore_transactions.csv`

One row per customer: a point-in-time usage and billing snapshot for the
`2026-05` billing month.

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `transaction_id` | string (key) | `T00001`-`T00280`. |
| `customer_id` | string (key) | Foreign key to the customers file. |
| `billing_month` | string (date) | `2026-05` for all rows (provenance field). |
| `storage_gb` | numeric | Storage consumed, GB. |
| `api_calls` | numeric | API calls in the month (values reach millions). |
| `seats` | numeric (int) | Licensed user seats. |
| `billing_amount` | numeric (USD) | Billed amount; equals MRR in the customers file. |

::: {.callout-warning}
## Standardise before clustering

`storage_gb`, `api_calls` and `seats` are on wildly different scales. Run them
through **Preprocess** (standardise) before **k-Means**, or `api_calls` will
dominate every distance calculation. The file clusters cleanly into about four
behavioural groups; joining the cluster id back to the customer profile tells
you who those groups are.
:::

## `cloudcore_support_tickets.csv`

One row per support interaction; multiple tickets per customer. Date range
June 2025 to May 2026.

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `ticket_id` | string (key) | `TK00001`-`TK00360`. |
| `customer_id` | string (key) | Foreign key to the customers file. |
| `product` | categorical (4) | `DataVault`, `Analytics Pro`, `CloudSync`, `Account`. |
| `region` | categorical (3) | Customer's region. |
| `date` | date (ISO) | Ticket date. |
| `channel` | categorical (4) | `Email`, `Portal`, `Chat`, `Phone`. |
| `satisfaction_score` | ordinal (1-5) | Post-resolution CSAT. |
| `ticket_text` | free text | Short customer message; tone tracks the score. |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Signal worth finding

Satisfaction is not uniform: one product and one region sit clearly below the
rest. The text column supports preprocess, TF-IDF, hierarchical clustering
(clusters track product) and sentiment analysis (compare model sentiment
against the recorded score). Requires the **Orange3-Text** add-on.
:::

## `cloudcore_reviews.csv`

One row per product review, roughly one per sampled customer. Free text plus a
clean ordinal label.

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `review_id` | string (key) | `R00001`-`R00240`. |
| `customer_id` | string (key) | Foreign key to the customers file. |
| `product` | categorical (3) | `DataVault`, `Analytics Pro`, `CloudSync`. |
| `region` | categorical (3) | Customer's region. |
| `rating` | ordinal (1-5) | Reviewer rating. |
| `review_text` | free text | Review body. |

::: {.callout-tip}
## Signal worth finding

Review sentiment tracks `rating`; one product reads clearly worse than the
others and the same under-performing region shows up here too. Text alone
partly separates happy from unhappy customers; check the first two principal
components coloured by rating.
:::

## A note on anonymisation

`company_name` is fabricated but realistic. No real person, email or address
appears anywhere in these files. Treat it as re-identifiable when you reason
about privacy: that is the point.
